# CHƯƠNG 16
# KHI QUYỀN NĂNG ĐƯỢC MỜI

## I — MỘT CÁI TÊN ĐƯỢC GỌI

Đường mảnh Lilith vạch trên đất vẫn còn sau một lần ngủ.

Không còn nguyên như lúc đầu.

Gió đã đẩy vài hạt bụi xuống rãnh. Một con vật nhỏ đi ngang để lại dấu chân cắt qua nó. Ở một đầu, Adam vô tình giẫm mất gần nửa đoạn khi mang cành cây về chỗ trú.

Lilith nhìn dấu chân ấy.

Nàng không sửa.

Có lẽ vì đường đó chưa bao giờ được tạo ra để trường tồn.

Nó chỉ từng có nghĩa trong một khoảnh khắc: nơi ánh sáng của Healiangel đủ gần để họ nhìn thấy anh, nhưng chưa đủ gần để làm mắt họ đau.

Sáng hôm ấy, Healiangel không xuất hiện.

Không ai đã hẹn rằng anh sẽ.

Adam nhìn lên vài lần.

Lilith thì không.

Nàng đang bận với một vấn đề khác.

Trong đêm, gió đã đi qua khu rừng mạnh hơn những ngày trước.

Không phải cơn cuồng nộ đủ để xé đất hay bẻ cả sườn núi. Chỉ là thứ gió khiến những cành già cọ vào nhau, những lá khô rời khỏi thân cây và một cây lớn ở gần dòng nước cuối cùng chịu thua sức nặng của chính nó.

Nó đổ ngang qua lối Adam và Lilith thường dùng để đi từ chỗ trú đến một khoảng đất có nhiều đá phẳng.

Thân cây lớn hơn vòng tay của cả hai cộng lại.

Một phía vẫn mắc trên gốc nứt.

Phía còn lại nằm sâu xuống nền đất mềm.

Adam đã thử đẩy.

Không nhúc nhích.

Lilith thử đào đất dưới thân cây.

Nó hạ xuống thêm.

Họ dừng.

Adam mang đến một cành dài hơn, đặt một đầu dưới thân cây và kê đá làm điểm tựa.

Cành cong.

Gãy.

Lilith nhìn hai đoạn gỗ.

Một thoáng, nàng nhớ đến cách Healiangel đã dùng một cành gãy để nói về thứ đau không nằm trên thân thể.

Nàng không nhắc.

Họ tìm một cành khác.

Lần này Adam chọn gỗ dày hơn.

Hai người cùng ấn.

Thân cây dịch được một khoảng nhỏ.

Rất nhỏ.

Nhưng có.

Adam nhìn Lilith.

Lilith nhìn khoảng đất vừa lộ ra.

Họ làm lại.

Lần thứ hai, hòn đá kê trượt khỏi vị trí.

Cành bật lên.

Adam lùi kịp.

Lilith đưa tay giữ vai cậu.

Không ai bị thương.

Cả hai đứng nhìn thân cây.

“Nặng,” Adam nói.

Lilith gật.

“Nặng.”

Nàng nhìn quanh.

Không phải để tìm một thiên thần.

Để tìm một cách khác.

Họ lấy những sợi dây thô đã bắt đầu biết xoắn từ thân cây mềm và sợi thực vật. Buộc quanh một phần thân gỗ. Kéo.

Sợi dây căng.

Thân cây không đi đâu.

Lilith đổi góc.

Adam kê thêm đá.

Họ thử lần nữa.

Một đoạn dây đứt.

Cả hai ngã ngửa xuống đất.

Adam nằm đó vài nhịp.

Rồi bật cười.

Lilith nhìn cậu.

Nàng cũng cười.

Không có gì bi thảm về thất bại ấy.

Chỉ là cái cây vẫn ở đó.

Và họ thì chưa biết phải làm gì tiếp.

Adam ngồi dậy.

Ánh mắt cậu đi về phía đường mảnh còn sót lại dưới những thân cây xa hơn.

Lilith thấy.

Nàng không phản đối.

Hai người đi tới.

Adam đứng trước đường đất.

Không có ánh sáng nào chờ phía bên kia.

Không có đôi cánh.

Chỉ có rừng.

Cậu nói:

“Healiangel.”

Không có gì xảy ra.

Adam nhìn Lilith.

Lilith nhìn trời.

Rồi nói lớn hơn:

“Healiangel.”

Không có luồng sáng đáp lại.

Không có cánh cửa vô hình mở ra.

Không có quyền năng nào bị cái tên kéo xuống.

Healiangel chỉ đang quan sát Eden và nhận ra họ đang gọi mình.

Anh quay về phía Michael.

“Chúng gọi ta.”

Michael đã thấy.

Lucifer cũng vậy.

Không ai nói rằng cái tên có sức triệu hồi.

Không ai ghi nó thành nghi thức.

Adam và Lilith đã đứng ở nơi họ từng gặp Healiangel và gọi một người họ biết.

Chỉ thế.

Healiangel thu ánh sáng quanh mình.

“Ta xuống.”

Michael nói:

“Đi.”

Healiangel bước vào Eden.

Anh xuất hiện xa hơn đường Lilith đã vạch.

Không dùng nó như luật.

Không mặc định khoảng cách hôm qua sẽ đúng cho hôm nay.

Lilith nhìn anh.

Healiangel đứng yên.

Nàng bước tới đường cũ.

Nhìn khoảng giữa hai bên.

Rồi gật.

Healiangel tiến đến gần hơn.

Dừng ở nơi họ đã cùng chấp nhận trước đó.

Adam chỉ về phía thân cây đổ.

“Cây.”

Healiangel nhìn.

“Ta thấy.”

Adam nói:

“Nặng.”

“Ta thấy.”

Lilith chỉ lên cao.

“Michael.”

Rồi:

“Lucifer.”

Healiangel nhìn nàng.

Lilith chỉ cái cây.

Sau đó chỉ lên cao lần nữa.

“Đến?”

Healiangel không trả lời ngay.

“Các ngươi muốn gặp họ?”

Adam gật.

Lilith cũng vậy.

Healiangel ngẩng lên.

Phía trên, Lucifer đã đứng thẳng từ trước.

Michael nói:

“Chúng gọi tên chúng ta.”

Lucifer đáp:

“Ta nghe.”

“Chúng muốn chúng ta xuống.”

“Ta cũng nghe điều đó.”

Michael nhìn chàng.

“Ngươi còn chờ gì?”

Lucifer nhìn xuống.

“Chỉ muốn chắc rằng lần này cả hai chúng ta đều nhớ vì sao mình xuống.”

Michael giữ ánh mắt một lúc.

Rồi gật.

“Nếu ngươi khiến chúng đau, hãy lùi.”

“Nếu chúng bảo ta đi?”

“Thì đi.”

Lucifer nhìn Michael.

“Còn ngươi?”

“Như nhau.”

Healiangel vẫn đợi bên dưới.

Hai luồng sáng bắt đầu hạ xuống.

Nhưng không ai trong số họ bước đến đường Lilith đã vạch.

Bởi đường ấy từng được đo bằng cơ thể của Healiangel.

Không phải Michael.

Không phải Lucifer.

Một giới hạn từng đúng cho một người không tự nhiên trở thành giới hạn của tất cả.

Adam nhìn thấy họ trước.

Hai hình dạng.

Cùng xa.

Cùng giữ ánh sáng thấp.

Không ai đi trước.

## II — MICHAEL VÀ LUCIFER

Michael hiện ra bên trái Healiangel.

Lucifer bên phải.

Cả hai đứng xa hơn anh.

Đôi cánh Michael được khép sát đến mức những đường sáng dọc theo lông cánh chỉ còn như kim loại bắt ánh bình minh.

Lucifer giảm ánh sáng sâu hơn nữa.

Việc ấy không làm chàng trở nên nhỏ bé.

Nếu có gì khác, sự cố gắng thu mình chỉ khiến Adam nhận ra chàng đang giữ lại một thứ rất lớn.

Adam nhìn Lucifer lâu hơn.

Lucifer nhận thấy.

Nhưng không bước tới.

Lilith nhìn Michael.

Từ thanh kiếm bên hông đến cách chàng đứng.

Michael cũng nhận ra.

Bàn tay chàng rời xa chuôi kiếm.

Không phải vì Lilith tỏ ra sợ.

Vì chàng không muốn một vật nàng chưa biết trở thành lời đầu tiên về mình.

Healiangel chỉ từng người.

“Michael.”

Adam:

“Michael.”

Michael gật đầu.

Rồi Healiangel:

“Lucifer.”

Lilith nói:

“Lucifer.”

Lucifer cúi đầu rất nhẹ.

Không sâu.

Không như nghi lễ.

Chỉ là một sự đáp lại.

Michael nói trước.

Không phải vì địa vị.

Mà vì Adam đang nhìn chàng.

“Adam.”

Cậu chạm ngực.

“Adam.”

Michael quay sang.

“Lilith.”

Nàng gật.

Lucifer nhìn cả hai.

“Các ngươi đã gọi chúng ta.”

Từ của chàng nhiều hơn lời Healiangel thường dùng.

Adam hơi cau mày.

Lucifer thấy.

Chàng dừng lại.

Rồi nói đơn giản hơn:

“Gọi tên.”

Adam gật.

“Lucifer. Michael.”

“Phải.”

Lilith chỉ khoảng đất giữa họ.

“Xa.”

Lucifer nhìn xuống.

“Phải.”

Nàng chỉ Healiangel.

“Gần.”

“Phải.”

Lilith nhìn Lucifer.

“Vì sao?”

Lucifer liếc Healiangel.

Anh không trả lời thay.

Lucifer nói:

“Ánh sáng ta… khác.”

Lilith vẫn nhìn.

Chàng nghĩ một lúc.

Rồi dùng chính từ nàng đã tìm ra hôm qua.

“Ta khác Healiangel.”

Nàng chấp nhận dễ hơn.

Michael nói:

“Ta cũng vậy.”

Lilith nhìn Michael.

Rồi nhìn đường cũ.

Nàng hiểu.

Đó chưa từng là một đường dành cho thiên thần.

Chỉ là dấu của một cuộc gặp.

Nàng bước một bước về phía Michael.

Michael không di chuyển.

Lilith dừng.

Không đau.

Thêm nửa bước.

Vẫn không.

Michael hỏi:

“Đủ?”

Lilith nhìn mắt mình như thể tự hỏi chúng.

Rồi gật.

Michael ghi nhớ bằng khoảng cách.

Lucifer không đợi nàng thử với chàng.

Chàng chỉ đất dưới chân.

“Ta ở đây. Được?”

Lilith nhìn khoảng cách.

Rồi gật.

Lucifer không tiến thêm.

Michael liếc chàng.

Lucifer thấy.

“Ngươi đang kiểm tra xem ta có nhớ không?”

Michael đáp:

“Có.”

“Ta đã nói ta sẽ đứng nơi họ bảo.”

“Và ta đã nói ta sẽ nhớ.”

Adam không hiểu phần lớn những lời ấy.

Nhưng cậu nghe thấy giọng hai người đổi khi nói với nhau.

Không giống cách Healiangel nói với họ.

Có thứ gì đó cũ hơn nằm giữa Michael và Lucifer.

Không phải thù địch.

Chưa.

Giống hai tảng đá từng nằm cạnh nhau đủ lâu để mỗi vết trầy trên một mặt đều có một dấu tương ứng ở mặt kia.

Adam chỉ thân cây đổ.

“Giúp?”

Michael nhìn sang.

Chỉ một lần nhìn, chàng đã biết mình có thể giải quyết việc đó dễ đến mức gần như không đáng gọi là sức lực.

Lucifer cũng biết.

Michael nói:

“Được.”

Lucifer nhìn chàng.

Michael chưa làm gì.

Nhưng Lucifer đã thấy câu trả lời đến nhanh thế nào.

“Khoan.”

Michael quay đầu.

Adam và Lilith cùng nhìn Lucifer.

Lucifer chỉ cái cây.

“Các ngươi muốn…”

Chàng tìm từ đơn giản.

“…chúng ta làm?”

Adam gật.

Michael nói:

“Họ vừa yêu cầu giúp.”

Lucifer vẫn nhìn thân cây.

“Giúp không phải lúc nào cũng là làm thay.”

Michael đáp:

“Ta chưa nói sẽ làm thay.”

“Ngươi đã chuẩn bị dời cả thân cây.”

Michael im một nhịp.

Đủ để Lucifer biết mình đoán đúng.

Michael nói:

“Nó chặn đường.”

Lucifer quay về phía Adam.

“Các ngươi muốn cây sang đó?”

Chàng chỉ sang một khoảng trống bên cạnh.

Adam lắc đầu.

Lucifer hơi nhướng mắt.

Michael nhìn Adam.

“Không?”

Adam bước về phía cái cây.

“Đến.”

Cậu gọi.

Ba thiên thần nhìn nhau.

Healiangel đi trước.

Michael và Lucifer theo sau.

Không ai nhận ra rằng chỉ trong vài nhịp, thế cân bằng đã thay đổi.

Lúc đầu Heaven xuống để được gặp.

Bây giờ Humanity đang dẫn đường.

## III — THỨ HỌ ĐÃ THỬ

Adam đưa họ đến cành gãy đầu tiên.

Sau đó cành thứ hai.

Đá kê.

Dây đứt.

Đất bị đào.

Những dấu chân hai người để lại quanh thân cây.

Lucifer cúi xuống nhìn.

Chàng chạm vào đoạn dây đứt.

Không dùng quyền năng.

Chỉ cầm nó lên.

“Các ngươi làm?”

Lilith gật.

“Làm.”

Adam chỉ cành gỗ dài.

“Đẩy.”

Rồi minh họa.

Lucifer hiểu.

Michael nhìn điểm tựa bằng đá.

“Đòn.”

Healiangel nhìn chàng.

Michael thấy.

“Ta gọi nó như vậy. Không phải họ.”

Lilith chỉ vết trượt trên đất.

“Không.”

Nàng dựng lại cành.

Đặt đá.

Ấn xuống.

Cành cong.

Thân cây nhấc lên một chút.

Rồi hạ xuống.

Michael nhìn chuyển động.

“Ta hiểu.”

Lucifer vẫn cầm sợi dây.

“Các ngươi muốn thân cây đi đâu?”

Adam chỉ một khoảng bên cạnh.

Không phải vứt đi.

Một phần đất ở đó thấp hơn.

Nếu thân cây được xoay, nó có thể nằm dọc theo mép nước thay vì chắn ngang lối.

Lilith lấy một cành nhỏ vẽ trên đất.

Một đường là vị trí hiện tại.

Một đường khác nghiêng sang bên.

Lucifer ngồi xuống để nhìn.

Michael vẫn đứng.

Lilith ngẩng lên nhìn chàng.

Rồi nhìn Lucifer.

Michael hiểu.

Chàng hạ mình xuống.

Năm sinh linh đứng quanh hình vẽ trên đất.

Không ai trong số họ nói về sự kỳ lạ của cảnh ấy.

Lilith chỉ phần gốc.

“Ở.”

Chỉ đầu bên kia.

“Đi.”

Adam chỉ các viên đá.

“Kê.”

Rồi chỉ thân cây.

“Lên.”

Healiangel hiểu trước.

“Họ không muốn dời nó hoàn toàn.”

Michael nhìn hình.

“Muốn nâng một phía để đặt đá.”

Adam gật mạnh.

“Đá.”

Lucifer nhìn Michael.

“Vậy nếu ngươi vừa nhấc toàn bộ thân cây—”

“Ta đã không làm.”

“Nhưng ngươi định.”

Michael không phản bác.

Lucifer đặt sợi dây xuống.

“Nếu mỗi khi họ gặp thứ nặng hơn sức mình, chúng ta chỉ cần—”

Michael cắt ngang:

“Họ đã tự thử.”

“Ta thấy.”

“Và họ yêu cầu giúp.”

“Ta cũng thấy.”

“Vậy vấn đề của ngươi là gì?”

Lucifer đứng lên.

“Ngày mai.”

Michael cau mày.

“Ngày mai?”

“Ngày mai một tảng đá lớn hơn. Sau đó một vách đất. Rồi một dòng nước. Nếu chỉ cần gọi tên chúng ta—”

“Ngươi nghĩ giúp họ một lần sẽ khiến họ quên cách làm?”

“Ta nghĩ sức mạnh có thể khiến một con đường trở nên quá dễ để người ta còn muốn nhìn những con đường khác.”

Michael nhìn Lucifer.

“Ngươi đang quyết định thay họ rằng khó khăn tốt cho họ.”

Câu nói làm Lucifer dừng.

Michael tiếp:

“Ngươi phản đối việc ta làm thay.”

“Phải.”

“Nhưng nếu họ yêu cầu giúp mà ngươi từ chối chỉ vì ngươi sợ họ sẽ lệ thuộc…”

Michael nhìn thẳng chàng.

“…thì ai đang quyết định thay họ?”

Lucifer không đáp ngay.

Một nét gì đó tối lại trong ánh mắt.

Không phải giận Michael.

Giận vì câu hỏi đã tìm đúng chỗ.

Healiangel quan sát hai người.

Adam và Lilith cũng vậy.

Nhưng với họ, cuộc tranh luận ngày càng xa khỏi cái cây.

Michael nói:

“Họ cần cái cây được nâng.”

Lucifer đáp:

“Ngươi lại đang nói họ cần gì.”

Michael khựng.

Lucifer cũng khựng.

Cả hai nhìn nhau.

Healiangel nói:

“Họ đã yêu cầu điều gì?”

Chỉ một câu.

Không giải thích.

Không kết luận ai đúng.

Michael nhìn Adam.

Lucifer nhìn Lilith.

Trong vài nhịp trước đó, cả hai đã tranh luận về tự do của Humanity—

mà không hỏi Humanity muốn điều gì.

Lilith chỉ thân cây.

“Giữ.”

Michael:

“Giữ?”

Nàng đặt hai tay dưới một cành nhỏ.

Nâng.

Giữ nó đứng yên.

Adam chèn một viên đá bên dưới.

Sau đó nàng thả.

Healiangel mỉm cười rất nhẹ.

Adam chỉ Michael.

Rồi Lucifer.

“Giữ.”

Chỉ mình và Lilith.

“Làm.”

Lucifer nhìn Michael.

Michael nhìn Lucifer.

Không ai nói thêm về ngày mai.

## IV — CHỈ GIỮ

Michael bước tới thân cây.

Lucifer đi về phía đối diện.

Healiangel vẫn đứng ngoài.

Không phải vì anh không thể giúp.

Bởi Adam và Lilith đã chỉ Michael và Lucifer.

Phạm vi của lời yêu cầu lần này đã đủ rõ.

Michael đặt một tay dưới phần thân gần gốc.

Michael nhìn chúng.

Lucifer cũng vậy.

Trong một thời gian rất dài, Heaven đã nghĩ về Nhân Loại như những sinh linh sẽ được phục vụ, được dẫn dắt, được bảo vệ khỏi những điều họ chưa hiểu.

Không ai trong số họ từng hỏi một câu khác.

Điều gì sẽ xảy ra nếu một ngày—

những sinh linh ấy quay lại?

Không phải để chống đối.

Không phải để quỳ xuống.

Mà để nhìn thấy một vết nứt trong những kẻ mạnh hơn mình—

và hỏi liệu họ có thể giúp.

Lucifer nhìn Adam.

Rồi Lilith.

Rồi Healiangel.

“Michael.”

“Gì?”

Lucifer không rời mắt khỏi họ.

“Có lẽ chúng ta đã nhìn lời ấy từ một phía quá lâu.”

Michael im lặng một lúc.

Chàng biết chàng đang nói về điều gì.

Nhưng Michael không nhìn lên Điện Ngai.

Không diễn giải sự im lặng.

Không gọi suy nghĩ ấy là Ý Chí.

Chàng chỉ nói:

“Có thể.”

Không nhiều.

Không đủ để trở thành doctrine.

Nhưng cũng không phải từ chối.

Dưới ánh chiều muộn, Adam và Lilith quay về phía cây cầu nhỏ mà chính họ đã chọn vị trí, chính họ đã kê đá, chính họ đã kéo dây—

và những quyền năng lớn hơn họ chỉ giữ phần trọng lượng mà họ đã yêu cầu.

Ba thiên thần đứng lại.

Không ai ra lệnh Humanity phải quay lại ngày mai.

Không ai hứa sẽ xuất hiện mỗi khi được gọi.

Không ai đặt một món nợ lên công việc vừa hoàn tất.

Khoảng cách giữa họ vẫn còn.

Nhưng nó đã thay đổi.

Ngày hôm trước, khoảng cách ấy được tạo ra để quyền năng không lấn át lựa chọn.

Hôm nay, nó đã đủ gần để quyền năng được mời vào—

mà không cần chiếm lấy công việc.

Và trước khi ngày tắt hẳn, Heaven nhận được từ Nhân Loại điều chưa ai từng dự liệu.

Không phải sự phục tùng.

Không phải lòng tôn kính.

Không phải một lời cầu xin.

Một lời đề nghị.

— HẾT CHƯƠNG 16 —

# CHAPTER 16
# WHEN POWER IS INVITED

## I — A NAME CALLED

The thin line Lilith had drawn in the earth survived one night.

Not unchanged.

Wind had filled part of its groove with dust. A small animal had crossed it, leaving prints through the mark. At one end, Adam had accidentally erased nearly half of it while carrying a branch back toward their shelter.

Lilith looked at the footprints.

She did not redraw the line.

Perhaps because it had never been made to last.

It had meant one thing in one particular moment: the place where Healiangel's light was near enough for them to see him clearly, but not near enough to hurt their eyes.

That morning, Healiangel did not appear.

No one had promised that he would.

Adam looked upward several times.

Lilith did not.

She had another problem to consider.

During the night, the wind had moved through the forest with greater force than before.

Not a storm fierce enough to tear open the earth or break a mountain. Only the kind of wind that made old branches grind together, stripped dry leaves from their stems, and finally persuaded one great tree beside the water to surrender to its own weight.

It had fallen across the route Adam and Lilith usually took between their shelter and a stretch of ground where broad, flat stones were plentiful.

The trunk was wider than both their arms together could encircle.

One end still rested against the split stump.

The other had sunk into soft earth.

Adam pushed.

Nothing.

Lilith dug beneath one side.

The trunk sank farther.

They stopped.

Adam brought a long branch, wedged one end beneath the trunk, and placed a stone under it.

He pushed down.

The branch bent.

Then snapped.

Lilith looked at the two broken pieces.

For an instant, she remembered Healiangel using a broken branch to explain a pain that did not belong to the body.

She said nothing.

They found another branch.

This one was thicker.

Together they pushed.

The trunk shifted.

Barely.

But it moved.

Adam looked at Lilith.

Lilith looked at the strip of exposed earth.

They tried again.

This time the supporting stone slipped free.

The branch sprang upward.

Adam moved back in time.

Lilith caught his shoulder.

Neither was hurt.

They stood and regarded the tree.

“Heavy,” Adam said.

Lilith nodded.

“Heavy.”

She looked around.

Not for an angel.

For another method.

They brought rough cords they had begun making from pliable bark and twisted plant fibers. They bound one around the trunk.

Pulled.

The rope tightened.

The tree remained where it was.

Lilith changed the angle.

Adam added another stone.

They pulled again.

One length of cord snapped.

Both of them fell backward.

Adam lay there for several breaths.

Then laughed.

Lilith stared at him.

A moment later, she laughed too.

There was no tragedy in the failure.

The tree was simply still there.

And they still did not know what to do with it.

Adam sat up.

His gaze moved toward the faint remains of the line Lilith had drawn the previous day.

Lilith noticed.

She did not object.

They went to it together.

Adam stood before the old mark.

There was no light beyond it.

No wings.

Only trees.

“Healiangel.”

Nothing answered.

Adam looked at Lilith.

Lilith looked upward.

“Healiangel.”

Again, the forest remained the forest.

No power had been compelled by the name.

Healiangel was simply watching Eden and recognized that they were calling for him.

He turned toward Michael.

“They are calling me.”

Michael had already seen.

So had Lucifer.

Healiangel drew his radiance inward.

“I will go.”

Michael said,

“Go.”

Healiangel descended into Eden.

He appeared farther away than the line Lilith had drawn.

He did not treat yesterday's boundary as a law.

Nor did he assume that yesterday's safe distance would necessarily remain today's.

Lilith saw him.

Healiangel waited.

She approached the faded line and looked across the space between them.

Then nodded.

Healiangel came closer and stopped at the distance they had previously accepted together.

Adam pointed toward the fallen tree.

“Tree.”

“I see it.”

“Heavy.”

“I see that too.”

Lilith pointed upward.

“Michael.”

Then,

“Lucifer.”

Healiangel looked at her.

She pointed toward the tree.

Then upward once more.

“Come?”

He did not answer immediately.

“You want to see them?”

Adam nodded.

Lilith did too.

Healiangel lifted his gaze.

Above them, Lucifer was already standing straighter.

Michael said,

“They called our names.”

“I heard.”

“They want us below.”

“I heard that as well.”

Michael looked at him.

“What are you waiting for?”

Lucifer glanced toward Eden.

“Only to make certain that this time we both remember why we are going.”

Michael held his gaze for a moment.

Then nodded once.

“If you hurt them, move back.”

“If they ask me to leave?”

“Leave.”

Lucifer looked at him.

“And you?”

“The same.”

Below, Healiangel was still waiting.

Two muted lights began to descend.

Neither Michael nor Lucifer approached the line Lilith had drawn.

That distance had been discovered with Healiangel.

Not with them.

A boundary that had been right for one person did not become the measure of all others.

Adam saw the two forms first.

They stood equally far away.

Both had dimmed themselves.

Neither moved ahead of the other.

## II — MICHAEL AND LUCIFER

Michael appeared to Healiangel's left.

Lucifer to his right.

Both remained farther away than Healiangel.

Michael's wings were folded so closely that the light along the feathers looked almost like sunlight running across metal.

Lucifer had dimmed himself even further.

It did not make him seem small.

If anything, the visible effort of restraint only made Adam more aware that something immense was being held back.

Adam watched Lucifer longer.

Lucifer noticed.

He did not move.

Lilith studied Michael.

Her gaze moved from the sword at his side to the way he stood.

Michael noticed that too.

His hand moved farther from the weapon.

Not because Lilith appeared frightened.

Because he did not want an object she did not understand to become the first thing she learned about him.

Healiangel gestured toward Michael.

“Michael.”

Adam repeated it.

“Michael.”

Michael inclined his head.

Then Healiangel indicated Lucifer.

“Lucifer.”

Lilith said,

“Lucifer.”

Lucifer answered with a slight lowering of his head.

Not deep.

Not ritual.

Only acknowledgment.

Michael spoke first.

Not because rank gave him the right.

Adam happened to be looking at him.

“Adam.”

Adam touched his chest.

“Adam.”

Michael turned toward Lilith.

“Lilith.”

She nodded.

Lucifer looked at them both.

“You called us.”

His words were more complex than Healiangel's had been.

Adam frowned slightly.

Lucifer noticed and simplified.

“Called our names.”

Adam nodded.

“Lucifer. Michael.”

“Yes.”

Lilith pointed to the ground between them.

“Far.”

“Yes.”

She pointed toward Healiangel.

“Near.”

“Yes.”

Lilith looked at Lucifer.

“Why?”

Lucifer glanced at Healiangel.

Healiangel did not answer for him.

“My light is… different.”

Lilith continued to watch.

Lucifer thought for a moment.

Then used the word she had found the day before.

“I am different from Healiangel.”

That she understood.

Michael added,

“So am I.”

Lilith looked at Michael.

Then at the old line.

She understood.

The mark had never been a boundary for angels.

It was a memory of one meeting.

She stepped toward Michael.

Michael remained still.

Lilith stopped.

No pain.

Another half-step.

Still none.

Michael asked,

“Enough?”

Lilith seemed to consult her own eyes.

Then nodded.

Michael remembered the distance.

Lucifer did not ask her to repeat the test with him.

He pointed toward the ground beneath his feet.

“I stay here. Good?”

Lilith studied the space.

Then nodded.

Lucifer did not advance.

Michael glanced at him.

Lucifer noticed.

“You are checking whether I remember.”

“Yes.”

“I said I would stand where they asked.”

“And I said I would remember.”

Adam did not understand all of the exchange.

But he heard something in the way their voices changed when they spoke to one another.

It was different from the way Healiangel spoke to them.

Something old lived between Michael and Lucifer.

Not hatred.

Not yet.

More like two stones that had rested beside one another for so long that every mark on one had left some answering trace on the other.

Adam pointed toward the fallen tree.

“Help?”

Michael looked.

One glance was enough.

He could solve the problem with so little effort that it barely deserved to be called effort.

Lucifer knew that as well.

Michael said,

“Yes.”

Lucifer looked at him.

Michael had not yet moved.

Still, Lucifer had seen how quickly the answer had come.

“Wait.”

Michael turned.

Adam and Lilith looked at Lucifer.

Lucifer pointed toward the tree.

“You want…”

He searched for simpler words.

“…us to do it?”

Adam nodded.

Michael said,

“They asked for help.”

Lucifer kept looking at the trunk.

“Help is not always the same as doing it for them.”

“I did not say I would.”

“You were about to move the whole tree.”

Michael was silent for one beat.

Long enough to answer the accusation.

“It blocks their path.”

Lucifer turned to Adam.

“You want the tree there?”

He pointed to an open space beside the path.

Adam shook his head.

Lucifer's brow lifted.

Michael looked at Adam.

“No?”

Adam walked toward the fallen tree.

“Come.”

The three angels looked at one another.

Healiangel moved first.

Michael and Lucifer followed.

None of them remarked upon what had just changed.

Heaven had descended because Humanity had asked to meet.

Now Humanity was leading the way.

## III — WHAT THEY HAD ALREADY TRIED

Adam showed them the first broken branch.

Then the second.

The supporting stones.

The severed cord.

The earth Lilith had dug away.

The marks of their feet around the trunk.

Lucifer crouched beside the broken rope.

He lifted it with his hand.

No power.

Only fingers.

“You made this?”

Lilith nodded.

“Made.”

Adam pointed toward the long branch.

“Push.”

He demonstrated.

Lucifer understood.

Michael looked at the stone they had used as a support.

“A lever.”

Healiangel glanced at him.

Michael noticed.

“I am naming what I call it. Not what they do.”

The distinction remained.

Lilith pointed to the mark where the stone had slipped.

“No.”

She rebuilt the arrangement.

Branch.

Stone.

Pressure.

The branch bent.

The trunk rose slightly.

Then fell again.

Michael watched.

“I understand.”

Lucifer still held the broken cord.

“Where do you want the tree?”

Adam pointed toward a lower stretch of ground beside the water.

They did not want it gone.

If rotated, the trunk could lie along the edge of the stream instead of blocking the route.

Lilith took a small stick and drew two lines in the soil.

One showed the tree as it lay.

The other angled away.

Lucifer sat beside the drawing.

Michael remained standing.

Lilith looked up at him.

Then toward Lucifer.

Michael understood and lowered himself.

Five beings gathered around two lines scratched into earth.

No one remarked upon the strangeness of it.

Lilith pointed to the end near the stump.

“Stay.”

Then to the other end.

“Go.”

Adam pointed to the stones.

“Under.”

Then the trunk.

“Up.”

Healiangel understood first.

“They do not want the entire tree moved.”

Michael looked again at the drawing.

“They want one side lifted so they can place stones.”

Adam nodded.

“Stone.”

Lucifer looked at Michael.

“So if you had lifted the whole trunk—”

“I did not.”

“But you intended to.”

Michael did not deny it.

Lucifer set the broken rope down.

“If every time they meet something heavier than themselves we simply—”

Michael interrupted him.

“They already tried.”

“I see that.”

“And then they asked us.”

“I see that too.”

“Then what is your objection?”

Lucifer rose.

“Tomorrow.”

Michael frowned.

“Tomorrow?”

“A larger stone. A broken bank. A stream they cannot cross. If all they need to do is call our names—”

“You think helping once will make them forget how to act?”

“I think power can make one path so easy that other paths cease to be considered.”

Michael studied him.

“You are deciding for them that difficulty is good.”

Lucifer stopped.

Michael continued.

“You object to me acting in their place.”

“Yes.”

“But if they ask for help and you refuse because you fear they may depend on us…”

Michael met his eyes.

“…who is deciding for them then?”

Lucifer did not answer immediately.

Something darkened in his expression.

Not anger at Michael.

Anger because the question had found its mark.

Healiangel watched them both.

Adam and Lilith did as well.

But for the Humans, the conversation had begun to drift farther and farther away from the tree.

Michael said,

“They need the trunk lifted.”

Lucifer replied,

“You are saying what they need again.”

Michael stopped.

So did Lucifer.

They looked at one another.

Healiangel asked,

“What did they ask us to do?”

Nothing more.

No ruling.

No declaration of who had been right.

Michael looked toward Adam.

Lucifer looked toward Lilith.

For several moments they had been arguing about Human freedom—

without asking the Humans what they wanted.

Lilith pointed toward the trunk.

“Hold.”

Michael repeated,

“Hold?”

She placed both hands beneath a small branch.

Lifted.

Held it still.

Adam pushed a stone beneath it.

Then Lilith released the branch.

Healiangel's mouth moved faintly.

Adam pointed first at Michael.

Then Lucifer.

“Hold.”

Then at himself and Lilith.

“Do.”

Lucifer looked at Michael.

Michael looked back.

Neither spoke about tomorrow.

## IV — ONLY HOLD

Michael approached the trunk.

Lucifer moved to the opposite side.

Healiangel stayed beyond them.

Not because he lacked the strength to help.

Because Adam and Lilith had pointed to Michael and Lucifer.

The request was clear enough.

Michael placed one hand beneath the section nearest the stump.

Lucifer took the lower side.

If either had used the strength with which Heaven had once shaped far greater structures, the tree might have left the earth before Adam could blink.

Neither did.

Michael looked at Lilith.

“How high?”

She did not understand.

He raised his hand slightly.

“High?”

Lilith showed him with her own hand.

“Here.”

Michael nodded.

Lucifer asked,

“Slow?”

“Slow.”

Adam stood beside the stones they had already prepared.

Healiangel watched them.

“Begin?”

Adam nodded.

Michael lifted first.

The tree gave a low wooden groan.

Lucifer held the other side so it would not roll.

Wet soil tore away from the bark.

Adam immediately pushed the first stone underneath.

“Stop.”

This time, the word came from Adam.

Michael stopped.

There was no weight in the voice beyond its meaning.

Lucifer stopped with him.

Lilith knelt.

She used a branch to clear soil from the support point.

Adam added another stone.

The trunk tilted.

Michael felt the weight shift.

He could have corrected it instantly.

He did not.

Lilith examined it.

Pressed with one hand.

“More.”

Michael lifted a little farther.

Lucifer changed his grip.

The trunk steadied.

Adam wedged another stone into place.

Lilith threaded the cord beneath the lower section.

They pulled.

Not enough.

Lucifer saw it.

His body almost answered before thought.

Then he stopped himself.

“Hold,” Lilith reminded him.

Lucifer looked at her.

“Yes.”

He only held.

Adam and Lilith pulled.

The cord tightened.

The end of the tree turned.

Adam lost his footing.

Healiangel took half a step.

Then stopped.

Adam caught himself with his hands and rose.

No injury.

No need for healing.

Healiangel moved back.

Michael noticed.

Lucifer did too.

Neither commented.

Adam returned to the cord.

On the second attempt, he and Lilith changed positions.

Lilith pulled lower.

Adam used the branch as a lever.

The trunk rotated farther.

Michael asked,

“Enough?”

Lilith examined the angle.

Shook her head.

“More.”

They continued.

The work was slow.

Almost absurdly slow beside the beings who were helping them.

Michael had carried far greater weights.

Lucifer had wielded force at scales Adam and Lilith did not yet have words to imagine.

Healiangel could see each muscle tightening in the Humans' arms.

Still, Michael and Lucifer held only what they had been asked to hold.

## V — THE STRENGTH NOT USED

When the trunk finally turned into the shallow channel Adam and Lilith had prepared, Michael began lowering it.

“Slow,” Lilith said.

Michael looked at her.

“I hear you.”

Lucifer said nothing.

The trunk settled into the earth.

Its weight struck the ground with a deep sound.

Birds rose from nearby trees.

Small circles moved across the water.

Adam released the rope.

Lilith sat down.

Both breathed hard.

Michael straightened.

He was not tired.

Neither was Lucifer.

The difference required no explanation.

Adam looked at his hands.

The cord had reddened them.

Healiangel saw.

He did not move closer.

Adam noticed his gaze and lifted one hand.

“No.”

Healiangel nodded.

“All right.”

A red mark was not a request for healing.

Adam smiled.

Healiangel returned it.

Lilith stood.

She walked through the newly opened path.

Turned.

Walked back through it again.

Nothing blocked the way.

She pointed at the trunk.

“Good.”

Michael looked at it.

“Good.”

Lucifer crouched beside one of the supporting stones.

He picked it up.

“You chose this?”

Adam nodded.

Lucifer pointed toward another.

“Why not this?”

Adam picked up the second stone.

Placed it beside the first.

It was rounder.

He set it down and pushed.

It rolled.

Then he took the flatter stone.

Pushed.

It remained in place.

Lucifer understood.

“Does not roll.”

Adam repeated,

“Does not roll.”

Lucifer looked at the stone a moment longer than necessary.

Not because the discovery was difficult.

Because Adam had discovered it without him.

Michael watched Lucifer.

“You seem pleased.”

Lucifer glanced at him.

“I am deciding whether you expected otherwise.”

Michael said nothing.

Lilith heard the change in their voices.

She did not understand every word.

But she knew Lucifer was close to smiling.

She looked at Michael.

“You not laugh?”

Lucifer turned sharply toward him.

Healiangel lowered his eyes.

Michael regarded Lilith as though she had presented him with a tactical problem.

“I do.”

Lilith waited.

Michael remained still.

Lucifer said,

“She is waiting.”

“I know.”

For a moment, nothing happened.

Then a very small smile appeared on Michael's face.

Brief enough that Adam nearly missed it.

Lilith did not.

She pointed.

“Yes.”

Lucifer laughed.

Michael's expression immediately settled.

Adam looked at the two of them.

Then imitated Lucifer's earlier tone.

“I do nothing.”

Healiangel laughed first.

Lucifer followed.

Michael did not.

But the corner of his mouth took longer than usual to become still again.

## VI — IF THEY CALL TOMORROW

While Adam and Lilith gathered the lengths of cord that could still be used, Michael moved a short distance away.

Lucifer followed.

Michael spoke quietly.

“You were right about part of it.”

Lucifer looked at him.

“I will remember that sentence.”

“Do not make me withdraw it.”

Lucifer was silent.

Michael looked back toward the tree.

“I would have moved the whole thing.”

“I know.”

“Too quickly.”

“Yes.”

Michael turned.

“You were wrong as well.”

Lucifer did not resist the statement.

“I know.”

Michael had not expected agreement so easily.

Lucifer watched Adam reconnecting a broken length of cord.

“I was thinking about what might happen tomorrow before asking what they wanted today.”

“You wanted to protect their ability to act for themselves.”

“Yes.”

“But if they know where they want help?”

“Then refusing on their behalf can still become choosing on their behalf.”

Michael said nothing.

Lucifer nudged a small stone with his foot.

It moved barely at all.

“Unpleasant.”

“What is?”

“You being right.”

Michael almost answered.

Then decided against it.

Lucifer looked at him.

“Do not keep it too long.”

“I am not.”

Michael looked toward the Humans.

“You spoke of tomorrow.”

“Yes.”

“If they call tomorrow?”

Lucifer thought.

The question was different now.

It was no longer whether help should be offered.

“I ask what they want.”

“And then?”

“I decide whether I can do it without harming them.”

Michael nodded.

“And if they only need a stone held?”

Lucifer glanced at the fallen tree.

“Then I hold the stone.”

Michael walked back toward the others.

Lucifer remained where he was for a beat.

On the other side, Healiangel watched Lilith trying to reconnect the cord.

She made a knot.

Pulled.

It slipped loose.

Healiangel did not reach for it.

Lilith tried again.

This time it held.

Healiangel nodded.

She pointed at him.

“Know?”

He examined the knot.

“I know several ways.”

Lilith asked,

“Why not say?”

Healiangel paused.

“You did not ask.”

Lilith looked at him.

Then at the cord.

“Now ask.”

A smile appeared on Healiangel's face.

He sat beside her.

He did not take the rope.

He pointed.

“Through here.”

Lilith moved it.

“Then around.”

She looped the cord.

Adam came closer.

Healiangel continued guiding without taking the work from her hands.

Not because every lesson had to be taught this way.

Because this time she had asked how to do it.

She had not asked him to do it for her.

Michael and Lucifer watched from a distance.

Lucifer said,

“He learns quickly.”

Michael answered,

“So should we.”

## VII — WHAT POWER DOES NOT KNOW

By the time the sun had changed its angle, the trunk lay where Adam and Lilith wanted it.

Part of it now followed the edge of the stream.

Adam stepped onto it.

The wood shifted slightly.

He spread his arms.

Lilith watched.

Then followed him.

Michael asked,

“What is this for?”

Adam pointed toward the other side of the shallow water.

“Cross.”

The stream reached only below a Human knee in most places.

Michael could simply have walked through it.

So could Lucifer.

Healiangel did not need the trunk either.

But Adam and Lilith had turned an obstruction into something else.

Michael looked at the wood.

“Bridge.”

Adam did not know the word.

Michael immediately added,

“That is what I call it.”

Adam tested the sound.

“Bridge.”

Lilith repeated it.

“Bridge.”

Michael nodded.

Lucifer glanced at him.

“You gave them a word.”

“I know.”

Adam looked at the trunk again.

“Bridge.”

Lucifer said,

“It appears they intend to keep it.”

Michael ignored him.

Lilith sat on the trunk with her feet hanging above the water.

She pointed at Michael.

“Strong.”

Michael nodded.

“Yes.”

Then Lucifer.

“Strong.”

Lucifer inclined his head.

“Yes.”

Then Healiangel.

“Strong?”

Healiangel thought.

“Different.”

Lilith nodded as though she had expected that answer.

She pointed at herself.

“Strong?”

Healiangel looked at her.

Michael looked too.

Lucifer remained silent.

Healiangel asked,

“What do you think?”

Lilith studied her hands.

The tree.

The cord.

The path they had opened.

Then nodded.

“Strong.”

Adam pointed at Michael.

“Strong much.”

Then at himself.

“Strong little.”

Healiangel was about to respond.

Lucifer spoke first.

“Different.”

Adam looked at him.

Lucifer picked up the round stone Adam had rejected.

Set it on the ground.

Pushed.

It rolled.

Then he picked up the flat stone.

Pushed.

It remained.

“Which is good?”

Adam pointed at the flat one.

Lucifer added,

“For holding the tree.”

Adam nodded.

Lucifer pointed at the round stone.

“And for rolling?”

Adam considered.

He placed the round stone beneath a small branch.

Pushed.

The branch moved more easily.

His face changed.

Lucifer smiled.

“There.”

He placed both stones side by side.

“Different.”

Not higher.

Not lower.

Not identical.

Only different uses for different forms of strength.

Michael watched him.

“Are you teaching them?”

“No.”

Lucifer pointed toward Adam, who was experimenting with another rounded stone.

“I gave him a question.”

Michael understood.

He did not object.

Lilith looked at Healiangel.

“What strong you?”

The question stopped him.

He could say healing.

But the word did not yet exist fully between them.

He touched a small scratch on his own arm.

Not enough to require power.

“Sometimes…”

Healiangel looked at her.

“…I can help a wound close. Or help a living rhythm hold when it is growing weak.”

Lilith studied the scratch.

Then him.

“You do?”

“I can.”

“For Adam?”

“If needed.”

“For Lilith?”

“If needed.”

She pointed at Michael.

“If needed.”

Then Lucifer.

“If needed.”

Lucifer said,

“You answered that one too quickly.”

Healiangel looked at him.

“I can answer more slowly next time.”

Lucifer's mouth curved.

Michael shook his head once.

## VIII — AND YOU?

When the three angels prepared to leave, Adam approached Healiangel.

He did not call.

He simply came to the distance they had already accepted together.

Healiangel looked at him.

Adam looked at his own hands, still red from the cord.

Then at Healiangel.

“You help.”

Healiangel nodded.

“A little today.”

Adam pointed at Michael.

“Help.”

Michael nodded.

Then Lucifer.

“Help.”

Lucifer said,

“I only held.”

Adam looked at him.

“Help.”

Lucifer went silent.

He did not correct him again.

Lilith came closer.

She pointed toward the trunk.

“We do.”

“Yes.”

She pointed at Michael and Lucifer.

“You hold.”

“Yes.”

She thought.

Then said,

“Together.”

Healiangel looked toward the tree.

“Together.”

The word remained between them longer than the others.

Michael heard it.

Lucifer did too.

Neither defined it.

Neither turned one shared task into a covenant.

It created no debt.

It erased no difference in power.

It simply described what had happened.

Adam looked at Healiangel.

Something in his expression changed.

Not curiosity about wings.

Not light.

Not Heaven.

His gaze moved toward the broken branches beside the fallen tree.

One of them was the lever that had snapped that morning.

Adam picked up both pieces.

Placed them beside one another.

Healiangel recognized the image before Adam spoke.

The day before, Healiangel had done the same thing.

One branch once whole.

Now divided.

A way of describing pain that did not exist in the flesh.

Adam pointed at the wood.

Then Healiangel's chest.

“Pain.”

Healiangel did not answer at once.

Lilith remembered.

“You hurt.”

It was not a question.

Healiangel looked at her.

“Sometimes.”

Adam pointed toward the tree they had moved.

Then Michael.

Lucifer.

Healiangel.

Then himself and Lilith.

He searched for words.

Lilith watched him.

Then looked at Healiangel.

“You help us.”

Healiangel nodded.

Lilith touched her own chest.

“We…”

Adam completed it.

“…help you?”

The world seemed to become still.

Michael did not move.

Lucifer did not smile.

Healiangel stood before the two Humans and discovered that he did not know where to place his hands.

The question was not:

Where do you hurt?

It was not:

Can we heal you?

They did not yet understand what his pain truly was.

They knew something simpler.

He had helped them.

Perhaps there might be something they could do for him.

Healiangel looked toward Michael.

Michael had no command.

He looked toward Lucifer.

Lucifer had no answer.

For the first time since descending, Lucifer chose not to speak first.

Healiangel turned back to Adam and Lilith.

“I…”

He stopped.

The day before, he had learned that not knowing was not an emptiness that had to be filled immediately.

But this time he did not say *I do not know.*

Because he knew one thing.

Their question had reached somewhere Heaven had never thought needed guarding.

Healiangel lowered himself.

Not kneeling.

Not submitting to Humanity.

Only sitting so that his eyes were level with theirs.

“Perhaps.”

Adam waited.

Lilith did too.

Healiangel looked at the broken branch.

“But not today.”

Lilith tilted her head.

“Later?”

Healiangel met her gaze.

“Perhaps.”

Adam nodded.

He demanded no promise.

Asked for no time.

He placed the two pieces of wood beside one another.

Michael looked at them.

So did Lucifer.

For a very long time, Heaven had imagined Humanity as beings who would be served, guided, protected from things they could not yet understand.

No one had asked the question facing them now.

What happened when those beings turned around?

Not to rebel.

Not to kneel.

But to notice a fracture in those stronger than themselves—

and ask whether they could help.

Lucifer looked at Adam.

At Lilith.

At Healiangel.

“Michael.”

“What?”

Lucifer kept his eyes below.

“Perhaps we have looked at those words from one side for too long.”

Michael was silent.

He knew which words Lucifer meant.

But he did not look toward the Throne.

He did not interpret the silence.

He did not name Lucifer's thought as the Will.

After a time, Michael said,

“Perhaps.”

Nothing more.

Not enough to become doctrine.

Not a refusal either.

In the late light, Adam and Lilith returned toward the small bridge whose position they had chosen themselves, whose stones they had placed themselves, whose cords they had pulled themselves—

while beings vastly stronger than they were had held only the weight they had been asked to hold.

Three angels remained behind.

No one ordered Humanity to return tomorrow.

No one promised to appear whenever a name was called.

No one placed a debt upon what had been done.

The distance between them still existed.

But it had changed.

The day before, distance had kept power from overwhelming choice.

Today, it had been near enough for power to be invited in—

without taking possession of the work.

And before the day ended, Heaven received from Humanity something none of them had anticipated.

Not obedience.

Not worship.

Not a plea.

An offer.
